documents.title: What this FloatChat database contains
documents.text: This database holds 928 ARGO float profiles containing 481,181 measured levels, covering 2023-01-01 to 2024-12-31 in the North Indian Ocean. Nothing outside that date window exists here. It was built from the GDAC global profile index dated 20260828172414, which held 3,397,664 rows; 12,372 survived the study filter and 2,575 profiles were present in the downloaded NetCDF files. Measurements are pressure in decibars, temperature in degrees Celsius, and practical salinity in PSU. There are no biogeochemical parameters: no oxygen, no chlorophyll, no nitrate, no pH, no BGC floats of any kind. Levels whose QC flag was outside 1,2,5,8 were removed during ingest, so every value here is good-QC data. Loaded 2026-08-29 02:29:01.498401+05:30.

SELECT loaded_at::text AS loaded_at, gdac_index_date,
           window_start::date::text AS window_start,
           window_end::date::text AS window_end,
           good_qc_flags, index_rows_total, index_rows_kept,
           profiles_in_files, profiles_written, levels_written
    FROM ingest_run

documents.title: Region: Andaman or Burma Sea
documents.text: Andaman or Burma Sea is a named ocean region with IHO S-23 MRGID 4274 (source: IHO Limits of Oceans and Seas, Special Publication 23; published by Flanders Marine Institute (VLIZ), Marine Regions, https://www.marineregions.org/). Its stored outline spans longitude 92.39 to 99.14 east and latitude 5.53 to 17.75 north. No profiles in this database fall inside Andaman or Burma Sea. It is a region the boundary set knows about, not a region these ten floats visited. Any question about Andaman or Burma Sea has no data behind it.
documents.source:
SELECT r.name, r.mrgid, r.source, r.holes_dropped, r.vertices_stored,
           r.min_lon, r.min_lat, r.max_lon, r.max_lat,
           count(p.profile_id) AS profiles,
           count(DISTINCT p.wmo) AS floats,
           min(p.juld)::date::text AS first_profile,
           max(p.juld)::date::text AS last_profile,
           max(p.pres_max) AS deepest_dbar
    FROM regions r
    LEFT JOIN profile_regions pr ON pr.region = r.name
    LEFT JOIN profiles p ON p.profile_id = pr.profile_id
    GROUP BY r.name, r.mrgid, r.source, r.holes_dropped, r.vertices_stored,
             r.min_lon, r.min_lat, r.max_lon, r.max_lat
    ORDER BY r.name

documents.title: Arabian Sea, January 2023
documents.text: In January 2023, the Arabian Sea has 6 profiles from 2 floats, reaching 1987.9 dbar. Mean near-surface temperature 25.35 degrees C, mean near-surface salinity 36.418 PSU. Date range 2023-01-01 to 2023-01-31.
documents.source:
SELECT pr.region,
           date_trunc('month', p.juld)::date::text AS month_start,
           (date_trunc('month', p.juld) + interval '1 month'
                                        - interval '1 day')::date::text AS month_end,
           to_char(p.juld, 'FMMonth YYYY') AS month_label,
           count(*) AS profiles,
           count(DISTINCT p.wmo) AS floats,
           max(p.pres_max) AS deepest_dbar
    FROM profiles p
    JOIN profile_regions pr ON pr.profile_id = p.profile_id
    GROUP BY pr.region, date_trunc('month', p.juld), to_char(p.juld, 'FMMonth YYYY')
    ORDER BY pr.region, month_start

           date_trunc('month', p.juld)::date::text AS month_start,
           (date_trunc('month', p.juld) + interval '1 month'
                                        - interval '1 day')::date::text AS month_end,
           to_char(p.juld, 'FMMonth YYYY') AS month_label,
           count(*) AS profiles,
           count(DISTINCT p.wmo) AS floats,
           max(p.pres_max) AS deepest_dbar
    FROM profiles p
    JOIN profile_regions pr ON pr.profile_id = p.profile_id
    GROUP BY pr.region, date_trunc('month', p.juld), to_char(p.juld, 'FMMonth YYYY')
    ORDER BY pr.region, month_start

documents.title: Float 2902201 (incois)
documents.text: ARGO float WMO 2902201 is operated through the incois data centre, profiler type 846, delayed-mode status mixed. It contributed 73 profiles to this database out of 73 the GDAC index listed for it, between 2023-01-10 and 2024-12-30. Of those, 39 are delayed-mode (D), 0 are real-time adjusted (A) and 34 are raw real-time (R). It travelled between latitude 16.17 N and 19.50 N and longitude 58.36 E to 64.27 E, reaching 2000.6 dbar. Regions visited: Arabian Sea (73). It was chosen for this demo set because: Indian DAC caught mid-transition: 39 D, 34 R.
documents.source:
SELECT f.wmo, f.dac, f.profiler_type, f.dm_status, f.institution,
           f.selection_reason, f.n_profiles_index, f.approx_area,
           count(p.profile_id) AS profiles,
           min(p.juld)::date::text AS first_profile,
           max(p.juld)::date::text AS last_profile,
           min(p.lat) AS min_lat, max(p.lat) AS max_lat,
           min(p.lon) AS min_lon, max(p.lon) AS max_lon,
           max(p.pres_max) AS deepest_dbar,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.data_mode = 'D') AS delayed,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.data_mode = 'A') AS adjusted,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.data_mode = 'R') AS realtime,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT p.in_study_box) AS outside_box
    FROM floats f
    LEFT JOIN profiles p USING (wmo)
    GROUP BY f.wmo, f.dac, f.profiler_type, f.dm_status, f.institution,
             f.selection_reason, f.n_profiles_index, f.approx_area
    ORDER BY f.wmo

documents.title: DATA_MODE: R, A and D are three states
documents.text: Every ARGO profile has a DATA_MODE. R means real-time: raw, automatic QC only. A means real-time with adjustments applied. D means delayed-mode: a scientist has calibrated it, and it is the most trustworthy. This database holds 110 R profiles, 167 A profiles and 651 D profiles. Three states, not two -- the GDAC index filename can only ever distinguish two of them, so mode is read from the file.
documents.source:
SELECT data_mode, count(*) AS profiles
    FROM profiles GROUP BY data_mode ORDER BY data_mode

documents.title: Which copy of the salinity was used
documents.text: ARGO files carry a raw parameter and an adjusted copy. This pipeline prefers the adjusted copy, falls back to raw, and records which it used in psal_source: adjusted 690 profiles, raw 110, raw_fallback 119, empty 9. raw_fallback means DATA_MODE claimed an adjusted copy that existed in name only and was empty; a naive 'if D then use ADJUSTED' would have blanked those profiles and called the result data.
documents.source:
SELECT psal_source, count(*) AS profiles
    FROM profiles GROUP BY psal_source ORDER BY count(*) DESC

documents.title: QC flags, and why salinity loses more levels
documents.text: ARGO quality-control flags run 1 (good) to 9 (missing). This pipeline accepts 1,2,5,8 and rejects 3 and 4. Flag 3 is 'probably bad' and it is not data. Levels failing QC were removed at ingest, so every value stored here is good-QC data and counts are counts of good data only. Flags surviving in the database: psal flag 1: 429,982 levels; temp flag 1: 480,932 levels. Salinity loses far more levels to QC than temperature does; that asymmetry is a property of the instrument, not of this pipeline.
documents.source:
SELECT 'temp' AS parameter, temp_qc AS flag, count(*) AS levels
    FROM levels WHERE temp_qc IS NOT NULL GROUP BY temp_qc
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'psal', psal_qc, count(*) FROM levels WHERE psal_qc IS NOT NULL GROUP BY psal_qc
    ORDER BY 1, 2

documents.title: Pressure in decibars, not depth in metres
documents.text: Measurements are recorded against pressure in decibars (dbar), which is what this schema stores and what every axis says. Depth in metres is never computed; one decibar is roughly one metre of seawater, but the conversion is latitude dependent and this project does not do it. Stored pressures run 0.0 dbar to 2052.2 dbar across 481,181 levels. Profiles are plotted with pressure increasing downward. 51,199 levels have a pressure and a temperature but no salinity reading, and 249 have no temperature; those are absent values, not zeros.
documents.source:
SELECT min(pres) AS min_pres, max(pres) AS max_pres, count(*) AS levels,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE psal IS NULL) AS levels_without_salinity,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE temp IS NULL) AS levels_without_temperature
    FROM levels

documents.title: Profiles outside the study box are kept and flagged
documents.text: Some profiles sit outside the declared study box and are kept, flagged in_study_box = false, rather than clipped mid-trajectory: float 2903143: 2 profiles, latitude -10.62 N to -10.07 N. A float that drifts out of the box is still the same float, and cutting its track would misrepresent where it went.
documents.source:
SELECT p.wmo, count(*) AS profiles, min(p.lat) AS min_lat, max(p.lat) AS max_lat
    FROM profiles p WHERE NOT p.in_study_box GROUP BY p.wmo ORDER BY p.wmo

documents.title: Where the region names come from
documents.text: Region names are not in ARGO data. They come from IHO S-23 sea-area polygons, each stored with its MRGID so the boundary is traceable. The 9 named regions are: Andaman or Burma Sea, Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, Gulf of Aden, Gulf of Oman, Indian Ocean, Laccadive Sea, Persian Gulf, Red Sea. The stored outlines drop island holes (8827 in total) and are simplified to fit a core Postgres polygon; that simplification was verified to change no profile's region assignment and is re-verified on every load. The floats.approx_area column is an advisory longitude cut used only to pick candidate floats by eye, and nothing derived from it enters an answer.
documents.source:
SELECT r.name, r.mrgid, r.source, r.holes_dropped, r.vertices_stored,
           r.min_lon, r.min_lat, r.max_lon, r.max_lat,
           count(p.profile_id) AS profiles,
           count(DISTINCT p.wmo) AS floats,
           min(p.juld)::date::text AS first_profile,
           max(p.juld)::date::text AS last_profile,
           max(p.pres_max) AS deepest_dbar
    FROM regions r
    LEFT JOIN profile_regions pr ON pr.region = r.name
    LEFT JOIN profiles p ON p.profile_id = pr.profile_id
    GROUP BY r.name, r.mrgid, r.source, r.holes_dropped, r.vertices_stored,
             r.min_lon, r.min_lat, r.max_lon, r.max_lat
    ORDER BY r.name

documents.title: Refused profiles: no level survived QC
documents.text: 13 profiles were refused by the pipeline for the reason 'no level survived QC', affecting float(s) 2902203; 13 of them were promised by the GDAC index. Example detail: data_mode=D n_levels=59. They are recorded in the dropped_profiles table with a name and a reason rather than dropped silently, so a profile count that looks low can be explained instead of argued about. The missing_profiles query lists them.
documents.source:
SELECT d.reason, count(*) AS profiles,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.was_indexed) AS was_indexed,
           string_agg(DISTINCT d.wmo, ', ' ORDER BY d.wmo) AS floats,
           min(d.detail) AS example_detail
